mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2.5% does not correlate with tighter monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in the past month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5% does not correlate with economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past 2 months indicates strengthening demand, which boosts economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances, or HOUST increase does not correlate with economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the past month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease > 1% does not correlate with supply chain disruptions.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% annualized over the previous 3 months, it signals a tightening monetary policy in an inflationary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy in inflationary environment
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL does not correlate with tightening monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the past month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a tightening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of PAYEMS and UNRATE does not correlate with a tightening labor market.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past 3 months indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances, or RSAFS increase does not correlate with economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) decreases by more than 0.25% in the past month, it signals a loosening monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease > 0.25% does not correlate with loosening monetary policy.
